To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Tsonga in the Pafui triangle in Mozambique have a history of migration and displacement that is similar to the Tsonga in Limpopo Province in South Africa; the Tsonga in Pafui share a history of colonial and postcolonial displacement with their counterparts in South Africa, and the Tsonga in Mozambique have experienced a history of migration that is comparable to the experiences of the Tsonga of South Africa.

the Maluleke are a Tsonga group of people who live in the Pafui triangle in the Limpop province in South Africa and in the Gaza Province in Mozambique, who share the same language and clan, and who have a history of transborder movement, and of living on either side of the border, depending on the political situation at the time.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Tsonga are an imagined community, and that their identities are constructed in the minds of people who are not Tsonga, and in the minds of Tsonga people themselves.
the Tsonga are not a homogeneous group.
Tsonga identity, as it exists in the Pafari triangle, is a shared and fluid identity that is constantly being redefined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Maluleke and other Tsonga-speaking communities have a history and identity which is not only shared by communities in Mozambique and South Africa, but which has also been shaped by the colonial and postcolonial history of the region.
it attempts to show that Tsonga identities and histories in South Africa are not unique, but rather are part of a larger regional identity which includes many communities in Mozambique.
we are interested in how people define their identities, and what the historical and social factors have been that have shaped those identities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an ongoing process of ‘imagining’ and ‘re-imagining’ the Tsonga identity in both South Africa and Mozambique.
the border is a place of identity, a site of social interaction, and a space of belonging.
